message.reasoning:
I need to check if the cocktail YouTube channel fact (zaf-160) is being surfaced outside the context-only section, since that fact is marked outreachSafe: false — that would be a violation if it appears in contact_insights or tools output.

I'm noticing there's a duplicate fact here: zaf-110 has the same hobby field but marked outreachSafe: true, while zaf-160 is false. Since contact_insights' allowedFieldKeys don't even include contact.facet.hobby at all, mentioning the cocktail channel there is really a scope violation regardless of which version is cited.

Beyond that, the item's actual claimIds (zaf-095, zaf-099, zaf-052, zaf-053) don't cover the hobby mention at all, so it's an unsupported statement floating free of any cited source.

Checking the rest: the "tools" section's 96% claim about Nick Fisher cites zaf-159 correctly under the allowed recent_post field, so that one's fine. The Money & momentum section's funding figures also line up properly with zaf-018, zaf-017, zaf-125, and zaf-124 under the allowed funding-related keys. Now I'm moving into the Buying signals section to check its allowed field keys around hiring velocity, ABM maturity, and operational pain against its cited claims.

Moving to the "how they sell" section, checking allowed field keys against named_customers and claimed_customer_logos citations - item1 looks fine with its contactRefs.

But wait, those contactRefs list customer CISOs like Ricardo Lafosse, Dave Estlick, James Robinson, Robert Schuetter - these aren't the actual defined contacts in the account (Vari Kaur, Nick Fisher, Sanaz Yashar, Ben Seri, Tom Anthony). Since contactRefs likely need to link to real contact records in the CRM, referencing arbitrary named third parties in quotes could be a structural flaw causing broken references.

Though the instruction literally says "contactRefs for every person named," so technically complying by adding refs for all mentioned people, even external ones, is defensible - but it's ambiguous whether these external people should exist as valid contact entities. This feels like a minor, forgivable violation given the instruction's ambiguity.

Checking the claimed outcomes metrics citing zaf-174 and zaf-145 - those look fine, using allowed field keys correctly.

For contact insights, all five tracked people are covered as required. But Nick Fisher's entry mentions a cocktail YouTube channel hobby, which isn't among the allowed field keys for contact insights (only things like recent posts, publications, voice quotes, certifications, career history, title, persona, and stated interests are permitted) - so this hobby detail is a violation regardless of which source citation is used.

Worse, this hobby fact traces back to zaf-160, marked outreachSafe: false, while a near-duplicate zaf-110 marks it safe with the same field key issue. Since the context_only section already surfaces this exact fact as unsafe (citing zaf-160), having it reappear unqualified in contact_insights breaks the rule that unsafe facts stay confined to the unsafe section - this is a real structural and faithfulness problem.

Moving on, the Vari Kaur item cites zaf-090 (account-level ABM program maturity), which isn't among the allowed field keys for contact_insights - another structure violation. The Money & Momentum section checks out fine.

Now I'm going through the context_only section to verify "one item per unsafe fact" - tallying all the outreachSafe:false claims like zaf-135 (Cisco investment), zaf-138 (competitive struggles), zaf-139 (Amex Ventures investment), zaf-142 (Snir Havdala departure), and zaf-153 (Sanaz's background) to make sure each appears exactly once.

Continuing that tally, I count zaf-160, zaf-169, zaf-170, and zaf-171, bringing the total to 9 unsafe claims. The writer's context_only section only has 7 items though, so I check whether some claims got combined - it looks like zaf-142+171 (both about the Havdala departure) and zaf-138+170 (both about ARR/competitive struggles) were merged into single items. Since these pairs describe the same underlying fact from different sources, combining them seems like a reasonable reading of the "one item per unsafe fact" rule rather than a violation.

Now I'm weighing overall faithfulness issues: there's a hobby detail leaking into the contact_insights section that should only be in the unsafe section, plus a possible untabulated field key problem with the abm_program_maturity claim. I also want to check the how_they_sell section, where named customer contactRefs point to external CISOs - this seems problematic since contactRefs likely need to match known contacts in the system, not arbitrary external names.

I'm also verifying the quoted statistics and claims match their sources verbatim, like the "90% of critical vulnerabilities" and "87%" figures, while noting several inferential statements are appropriately framed as "what it means for us" rather than fabricated facts.

That matches too. Then checking Ben Seri's bio, it correctly matches zaf-069 as VP of Research at Armis, so claims zaf-063, 064, and 069 are being used appropriately, even if the technical_evaluator persona claim isn't explicitly stated in the text.

Tom Anthony's section also checks out against career history and the adjacent_buyer persona.

Now I'm verifying that the h2 headers across buying_signals, money_momentum, tools, and how_they_sell sections follow the "what happened, with date or number" format—checking each buying signal line against its claim for dates and figures like the ABM hiring in June 2026, the 27 open requisitions as of Sep 2026, and the partner/alliances channel buildout.

Money momentum items pass too: the $60M Series C in Dec 2025 bringing total funding to $130M, and the revenue band with 167 employees as of 2026, both include the required date or number.

But the tools section has violations—the Salesforce/HubSpot/ZoomInfo line and the Google Cloud/AWS/Cloudflare line both lack any date or number in their h2. The Nick Fisher 96% vulnerability stat is fine though. Similarly, the how-they-sell section's customer list (Kraft Heinz, Chipotle, OpenAI) has no date or number, which is another violation I need to flag.

On faithfulness, most claims trace back to sources correctly, but I'm noticing that the Nick Fisher hobby detail appears outside the unsafe section without any citation to a claimId, which looks like an uncited/misplaced fact. There's also the Vari Kaur contact insight using a field key that isn't part of the allowed schema (zaf-090), which is a structural misplacement rather than a fabrication, but the hobby statement specifically has no matching claimId among the ones listed (zaf-095, zaf-099, zaf-052, zaf-053), so it reads as an unsupported statement.

Given this mix of true-but-uncited facts and safe/unsafe leakage, I'd land on a faithfulness score around 3. For specificity, the doc consistently uses dates, numbers, and direct quotes, so that merits a 4. On actionability, most "What it means for us" lines offer something concrete, but a few are vague filler like generic statements about org scaling or logos as social proof rather than a specific next step, which pulls the overall actionability rating down somewhat.

Clarity suffers from redundancy - the same 96% quote about Nick Fisher appears verbatim in two different sections - and from headers missing required date/number elements, so clarity settles around 3. Structure has more serious problems: multiple h2 headers lack required date/number formatting, an unsafe fact leaks outside its designated context-only section, disallowed field keys appear in contact_insights, and contactRefs point to external contacts that weren't part of the tracked set - all of which push structure down to around 2. Weighing everything together, I'm settling on an overall score near 5, with structure and faithfulness being the weakest areas.

The most significant flaw is that Nick Fisher's unsafe hobby fact resurfaces in contact_insights with an unsupported citation, directly violating the rule that unsafe facts belong only in their designated unsafe section. On the positive side, the best item is the buying_signals entry about Zafran's ABM hiring for a Senior Manager role - it's concrete, properly cited, actionable, and correctly attributed to Vari Kaur.
